title: Nonzero differential detects generic etaleness for smooth curves
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X,Y$ be smooth curves over $k$, meaning separated integral schemes of finite type over $k$ of dimension one [def-pc-curve, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of a $k$-scheme $Z$, the sheaf $\Omega_{Z/k}$ is the sheaf associated with the module $\Omega_{B/k}$ of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. For every $k$-morphism $h:X\to Y$, the induced morphism of sheaves $dh:h^*\Omega_{Y/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}$, defined on local functions by $da\mapsto d(h^\sharp a)$, is nonzero if and only if there is a nonempty open subscheme $V\subseteq X$ such that $h|_V:V\to Y$ is étale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Here $h^*$ is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-smooth-curve-cotangent-generic-isomorphism] to $h$ and its canonical differential $dh$. Its source and target are line bundles, and $dh\ne0$ gives a nonempty affine open $V$ on which $dh$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation], $h$ and its source-open restrictions are locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type; smoothness supplies the finite-presentation and finite-type hypotheses on the structure maps.

By [lem-a1-differential-sheaf-transitivity-exact], on this $V$ the cokernel of $dh$ is exactly $\Omega_{V/Y}$, so it vanishes. The affine zero-differential characterization in [def-weil-unramified-morphism], with local finite type from Step 1, therefore makes $h|_V$ unramified.

Apply [lem-a1-unramified-curve-map-nonconstant] to obtain that $V$ is a curve and $h|_V$ has at least two image points. The target $Y$ is normal by [lem-sc-smooth-normal]. Thus [lem-a1-nonconstant-normal-curve-map-flat] makes $h|_V$ flat. Step 1 supplies local finite presentation; Step 2 supplies unramifiedness. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $h|_V$ is étale.

Conversely, suppose $h|_V$ is étale on a nonempty source open. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] it is unramified, and [def-weil-unramified-morphism] makes its affine differential modules zero. By [lem-a1-differential-sheaf-transitivity-exact], $dh|_V$ is then surjective onto $\Omega_{X/k}|_V$. Choose $x\in V$; [lem-a1-smooth-curve-cotangent-generic-isomorphism] makes this stalk free of rank one over the nonzero local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. A zero map cannot surject onto it, since its basis element $1$ is nonzero. Hence $dh|_V\ne0$ and $dh\ne0$. No properness, finiteness of $h$, perfectness of $k$, or rational point was required.

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.Hom.cotangentMap_ne_zero_iff_exists_etale_open {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegralCurve pX] [IsIntegralCurve pY] [Smooth pX] [Smooth pY] (h : X ⟶ Y) (w : h ≫ pY = pX) : h.cotangentMap pX pY w ≠ 0 ↔ ∃ V : X.Opens, (V : Set X).Nonempty ∧ Etale (V.ι ≫ h)
